questions.question: In March 2025, which region was announced as the site for the world’s first high-altitude para sports centre to boost preparations for the 2028 Paralympics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Leh, Ladakh**__.

__
 
• In March 2025, the region of **Leh, Ladakh** was announced as the site for the world's first high-altitude para sports centre.
 
• The initiative aims to boost preparations for the **2028 Paralympics**, enhancing India's global competitiveness in para-sports.
 
• The high-altitude environment in Leh is ideal for training athletes, as it helps improve **endurance and performance** by acclimatizing them to challenging conditions.
 
• The centre will also focus on **training, rehabilitation, and research** for para-athletes, making it a hub for innovation in para-sports.
 
• This project reflects India's commitment to developing infrastructure for para-sports and promoting inclusivity in athletics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Leh, Ladakh:**

 
 
• Situated at an altitude of approximately 3,500 meters above sea level, Leh is known for its challenging terrain and high-altitude environment.
 
• The region provides natural conditions that mimic high-performance training environments, essential for athletes preparing for international competitions.
 
 
 
• **Paralympics:**
 
 
• The Paralympics is a major international multi-sport event involving athletes with disabilities.
 
• The 2028 Paralympics will be held in **Los Angeles, USA**.
 
 
 
• **High-altitude Training Benefits:**
 
 
• Training at high altitudes increases red blood cell production, improving oxygen delivery to muscles.
 
• This enhances **athletic performance and endurance**, especially in endurance sports.
 
 
 
• **India's Para-sports Development:**
 
 
• India has been investing in para-sports infrastructure and athlete development to improve its global standing.
 
• Initiatives like the high-altitude centre in Leh signify a strong push towards inclusivity and excellence in sports.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India prevents any child below the age of 14 years from being employed in the factory, mine or hazardous occupation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 24**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 24** of the Constitution of India prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in factories, mines, or any hazardous occupations.
 
• This provision is part of the fundamental rights under the **Right against Exploitation** outlined in the Constitution.
 
• The article aims to protect children from exploitation and hazardous working conditions that can harm their physical and mental health.
 
• It aligns with the government's commitment to ensuring the welfare and development of children by preventing child labor in unsafe environments.
 
• India has ratified international conventions such as the **UN Convention on the Rights of the Child** and the **ILO Convention No. 182** to combat child labor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Child Labor Prohibition and Regulation Act, 1986:**

 
 
• This act regulates the working conditions for children and prohibits their employment in hazardous occupations.
 
• It defines hazardous occupations and processes where child labor is strictly prohibited.
 
 
 
• **The Right to Education Act, 2009:**
 
 
• This act ensures free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years, thereby indirectly combating child labor.
 
• Education is seen as a key tool to prevent children from being exploited in the workforce.
 
 
 
• **National Child Labor Project (NCLP):**
 
 
• Under this initiative, children withdrawn from hazardous work are enrolled in special schools to provide education, nutrition, and vocational training.
 
• The program aims to rehabilitate child laborers and integrate them into the mainstream education system.
 
 
 
• **International Initiatives:**
 
 
• India is a signatory to the **ILO Minimum Age Convention (No. 138)**, which sets the minimum age for employment.
 
• The **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** also emphasize the elimination of child labor under Goal 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth).

questions.question: The 'Drain of Wealth' theory, which highlighted the economic exploitation of India under British rule, was prominently advocated by whom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadabhai Naoroji**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji was an Indian political leader, educator, and economist who is famously known as the **'Grand Old Man of India.'**
 
• He introduced the 'Drain of Wealth' theory in his book **"Poverty and Un-British Rule in India,"** published in 1901.
 
• The theory highlighted how the British systematically drained India's wealth and resources for their economic benefit.
 
• Naoroji was the first Indian to become a member of the British Parliament, where he actively raised concerns about the economic exploitation of India.
 
• The 'Drain of Wealth' theory became a cornerstone for the Indian freedom movement, influencing leaders like Mahatma Gandhi and Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Aspects of the 'Drain of Wealth' Theory:**

 
 
• The theory argued that a significant portion of India's wealth was being transferred to Britain in the form of **home charges** (administrative expenses and pensions).
 
• Export of raw materials and the import of finished goods from Britain created a massive trade imbalance.
 
• Indian taxpayers funded the salaries and pensions of British officials, further depleting the country's resources.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Theory:**
 
 
• The theory exposed the economic exploitation of India under British rule, fueling nationalist sentiments.
 
• It provided a strong economic argument for independence and self-rule.
 
 
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji's Other Contributions:**
 
 
• He co-founded the **Indian National Congress (INC)** in 1885, which later became the primary political platform for India's independence struggle.
 
• He was the first Indian to be elected to the British House of Commons in 1892 as a Liberal Party candidate.
 
 
 
• **Other Advocates of Economic Nationalism:**
 
 
• While Naoroji introduced the 'Drain of Wealth' theory, other leaders like Gopal Krishna Gokhale and R.C. Dutt also highlighted the economic impact of British policies.

questions.question: In October 2024, the Mediation Act, 2023 came into force. What is a key feature introduced by this legislation?

options.text: It replaces arbitration and conciliation with mediation as the sole dispute resolution method.
It mandates that all mediation proceedings must be conducted only by retired judges.
It abolishes the role of mediators in public sector disputes.
It makes mediation compulsory for all civil and commercial disputes before court proceedings.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It makes mediation compulsory for all civil and commercial disputes before court proceedings**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Mediation Act, 2023 introduces **mandatory pre-litigation mediation** for civil and commercial disputes, aiming to reduce the burden on courts.
 
• This legislation promotes a **time-bound dispute resolution mechanism**, ensuring faster settlements through mediation.
 
• The Act establishes a **Mediation Council of India** to regulate the conduct of mediators and mediation institutions.
 
• It provides legal recognition to **mediated settlement agreements**, making them enforceable as court decrees.
 
• The Act encourages participation of trained mediators, ensuring professional and impartial facilitation in dispute resolution processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mediation:**

 
 
• Mediation is a voluntary and collaborative process where disputing parties work with a neutral third party (mediator) to resolve their issues.
 
• It differs from arbitration as it does not involve binding decisions made by a third party.
 
 
 
• **Mediation Council of India:**
 
 
• Established under the Mediation Act, 2023, the council oversees the accreditation of mediators and mediation service providers.
 
• It aims to standardize mediation practices across India.
 
 
 
• **Mediated Settlement Agreements:**
 
 
• These agreements, reached through mediation, carry legal enforceability under the Act.
 
• They are treated as final and binding, similar to court decrees.
 
 
 
• **Pre-litigation Mediation:**
 
 
• This process requires disputing parties to attempt mediation before approaching the court.
 
• It helps in reducing litigation costs and court congestion.

questions.question: Which version of Windows introduced the Start menu?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Windows 95**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Windows 95** was the first version of the Windows operating system to introduce the Start menu, a revolutionary feature for navigation.
 
• The Start menu combined the list of installed programs with quick access to system settings, making it user-friendly and efficient.
 
• It was launched on **August 24, 1995**, and marked a significant shift towards graphical user interfaces (GUI).
 
• The Start button, located at the bottom-left corner of the screen, became a hallmark of Windows operating systems.
 
• This version also introduced other innovations like the taskbar, long file names, and built-in support for plug-and-play hardware.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Windows Operating System:**

 
 
• Windows is a family of operating systems developed by Microsoft, designed for personal computers, tablets, and embedded systems.
 
• It is one of the most widely used operating systems globally, with billions of active installations.
 
 
 
• **Graphical User Interface (GUI):**
 
 
• The GUI allows users to interact with electronic devices through visual indicators like icons and buttons instead of text-based interfaces.
 
• Windows 95 was a major step forward in popularizing GUI for mainstream computer users.
 
 
 
• **Taskbar:**
 
 
• The taskbar, introduced in Windows 95, allows users to see and switch between open applications easily.
 
• It is located at the bottom of the screen and includes the Start button, quick launch icons, and the system clock.
 
 
 
• **Plug and Play (PnP):**
 
 
• Windows 95 introduced built-in support for PnP, allowing hardware devices to be automatically recognized and configured by the operating system.
 
• This feature greatly simplified the process of adding new hardware to a computer.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Start Menu:**
 
 
• The Start menu became an iconic feature of Windows, evolving through subsequent versions like Windows XP, Windows 7, and Windows 10.
 
• It remains a central element for accessing applications and settings in modern Windows systems.

questions.question: The Palk Strait separates India from which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sri Lanka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Palk Strait **is a narrow stretch of water separating **India and Sri Lanka**.
 
• It **connects the Bay of Bengal **in the northeast **with the Gulf of Mannar **in the southwest.
 
• On the Indian side, the Palk Strait borders the state of Tamil Nadu, while on the Sri Lankan side, it borders the Northern Province.
 
• Adam's Bridge (also known as Ram Setu), a chain of limestone shoals, lies within the Palk Strait and historically connected India to Sri Lanka.
 
• The Palk Strait is named after Robert Palk, a British governor of Madras during the 18th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geography of the Palk Strait:**

 
 
• The strait is approximately 40 to 85 miles (64 to 137 km) wide.
 
• It is relatively shallow, making navigation challenging for large ships.
 
 
 
• **Adam's Bridge (Ram Setu):**
 
 
• A chain of natural limestone shoals, believed to have formed naturally.
 
• It holds mythological significance in the Indian epic Ramayana as the bridge built by Lord Rama’s army to reach Lanka.
 
 
 
• **Economic and Strategic Importance:**
 
 
• The strait supports fishing and trade activities between India and Sri Lanka.
 
• It holds strategic importance for maritime routes in the Indian Ocean region.
 
 
 
• **Marine Biodiversity:**
 
 
• The Palk Strait is home to diverse marine life, including fish, crustaceans, and seaweed.
 
• Efforts are being made to preserve its unique ecosystem due to overfishing and habitat destruction.

questions.question: Which of the following was the final court of appeal for India under British rule?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Privy Council in London**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Privy Council in London served as the **highest court of appeal** for India during British rule.
 
• It was established as the final judicial authority to resolve disputes from colonies, including India, under the British Empire.
 
• Indian cases were appealed to the Privy Council after decisions from the Federal Court or provincial courts under colonial judicial hierarchy.
 
• The Privy Council's decisions were binding and considered the ultimate authority in legal matters during British rule.
 
• After independence, the jurisdiction of the Privy Council over Indian cases was abolished with the enactment of the **Federal Court (Enlargement of Jurisdiction) Act, 1948**, and later replaced by the Supreme Court of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Federal Court of India**

 
 
• Established in 1937 under the **Government of India Act, 1935** to function as India's highest court below the Privy Council.
 
• It dealt with disputes between provinces and the central government and had appellate jurisdiction over certain cases.
 
• Its role was significant but limited compared to the Privy Council.
 
 
 
• **Privy Council's Role**
 
 
• The Privy Council was composed of legal experts and judges in London.
 
• It played a crucial role in shaping colonial law and ensuring uniformity in legal decisions across British territories.
 
 
 
• **Abolition of Privy Council Appeals**
 
 
• Post-independence, the appeals to the Privy Council were abolished through legislative measures.
 
• The Supreme Court of India became the highest judicial authority in the country.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court of India**
 
 
• Established on January 28, 1950, as the apex court of India under the Constitution.
 
• It replaced the Federal Court and took over the judicial functions previously held by the Privy Council.

questions.question: Which file format is used for saving MS PowerPoint templates?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**.potx**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **.potx** file format is used for saving **MS PowerPoint templates**, which store pre-designed slides and layouts for presentations.
 
• It is a part of the **Office Open XML file formats** introduced in Microsoft Office 2007 and later versions.
 
• Templates saved in .potx format allow users to create new presentations with consistent designs and formatting.
 
• **.potx files are XML-based**, making them more efficient and easier to integrate with other applications compared to older formats.
 
• Unlike .pptx (presentation files), .potx files are specifically designed to be reused as templates for multiple presentations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **.pptx File Format:**

 
 
• Used for saving regular PowerPoint presentations.
 
• Supports multimedia elements like images, audio, and video.
 
• Introduced with Microsoft Office 2007 and uses XML-based compression.
 
 
 
• **.ppsm and .ppsx File Formats:**
 
 
• .ppsm files enable macro-enabled presentations.
 
• .ppsx files save presentations that directly open in slideshow mode.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between .potx and .pptx:**
 
 
• .potx files are templates for creating new presentations, while .pptx files are standalone presentations.
 
• .potx files ensure consistency across presentations based on the same template.
 
 
 
• **Office Open XML Formats:**
 
 
• Introduced in Microsoft Office 2007.
 
• Includes file formats like .docx, .xlsx, .pptx, and .potx.
 
• Offers better compression, integration, and data recovery than legacy formats.

questions.question: What type of majority is required to pass laws under Articles 2 and 3, as per Article 4(2) in Indian parliament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Simple majority**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Articles 2 and 3** of the Indian Constitution deal with the admission or establishment of new states and the alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states.
 
• As per **Article 4(2)**, laws made under Articles 2 and 3 require only a **simple majority** in Parliament, not a special or two-thirds majority.
 
• A **simple majority** means that the majority of members present and voting in each house of Parliament is sufficient to pass the law.
 
• Unlike constitutional amendments (which often require special or two-thirds majorities), these laws are considered ordinary legislation.
 
• This provision ensures flexibility in reorganizing states to address administrative and political needs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Simple Majority:**

 
 
• A simple majority is achieved when more than 50% of the members present and voting support a motion.
 
• This is the most commonly used voting method for passing ordinary bills in Parliament.
 
• It excludes abstentions and absent members from the total count.
 
 
 
• **Special Majority:**
 
 
• A special majority requires a higher threshold, such as two-thirds of the members present and voting, or in some cases, two-thirds of the total membership of the house.
 
• It is typically required for constitutional amendment bills under Article 368.
 
 
 
• **State Reorganization:**
 
 
• State reorganization involves altering the boundaries, names, or areas of states to address linguistic, cultural, or administrative concerns.
 
• Examples include the formation of Telangana in 2014 and the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Articles 2 and 3:**
 
 
• Article 2 allows Parliament to admit new states or establish new states on terms it deems fit.
 
• Article 3 enables the reorganization of states through changes in boundaries, areas, and names.
 
 
 
• **Article 4(2):**
 
 
• It specifies that laws made under Articles 2 and 3 are not considered constitutional amendments.
 
• Thus, they can be enacted through a simple majority, unlike constitutional amendment bills.

questions.question: Which bacterial disease is specifically confirmed by a serological method?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Typhoid**__.

*__Key Points__

__
 
• **Typhoid** is a bacterial infection caused by Salmonella typhi*, which spreads through contaminated food and water.
 
• The disease is commonly diagnosed using the **Widal test**, a serological test that detects antibodies against *S. typhi* antigens.
 
• The Widal test evaluates the presence of **O (somatic) and H (flagellar) antigens** in the blood, which are specific to typhoid fever.
 
• This method is preferred in areas with limited access to advanced diagnostic tools and is widely used for diagnosing typhoid in endemic regions.
 
• While the Widal test is widely used, its results must be interpreted cautiously alongside the patient’s clinical history and other diagnostic findings.

***Additional Information__**

 
• **Widal Test:**

 
 
• Developed in 1896 by Georges-Fernand Widal, it remains one of the most common methods to diagnose typhoid fever.
 
• A fourfold increase in antibody titers in two consecutive samples taken 7–10 days apart confirms the diagnosis of typhoid.
 
• False-positive results may occur due to previous infections or vaccination with S. typhi*.
 
 
 
• **Other Diagnostic Methods for Typhoid:**
 
 
• Blood Culture: The most reliable method, especially in the early stages of the disease.
 
• Bone Marrow Culture: Considered the most sensitive diagnostic method but is invasive and rarely used.
 
• Typhidot Test: A rapid diagnostic test that detects IgM and IgG antibodies specific to typhoid.
 
 
 
• **Symptoms of Typhoid:**
 
 
• High fever, abdominal pain, weakness, headache, loss of appetite, and constipation or diarrhea.
 
• In severe cases, it can lead to intestinal perforation and sepsis.
 
 
 
• **Prevention of Typhoid:**
 
 
• Vaccination: Typhoid conjugate vaccines and oral live-attenuated vaccines are available.
 
• Ensure safe drinking water, proper sanitation, and hygiene to prevent transmission.

questions.question: Samudrayaan, scheduled for 2026, involves which of the following?
questions.solution:

• The submersible, named **MATSYA 6000**, is designed to carry three people and is equipped with advanced scientific instruments for deep-sea exploration.
 
• The mission is set to be completed by **2026** and aims to study deep-sea biodiversity, mineral resources, and the impact of climate change on the ocean ecosystem.
 
• Samudrayaan will position India among the elite nations like the USA, Russia, Japan, France, and China that have developed deep-sea manned submersible technologies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The mission consists of multiple components, including deep-sea mining, underwater robotics, and research on marine biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **MATSYA 6000 Submersible:**
 
 
• MATSYA 6000 is an indigenously developed deep-sea submersible capable of diving to depths of 6,000 meters.
 
• It features a titanium alloy sphere to withstand extreme pressure and advanced imaging systems for underwater research.
 
 
 
• **Potential Benefits:**
 
 
• Exploration of polymetallic nodules, which are rich in minerals like manganese, nickel, cobalt, and copper.

• Countries like the USA (Alvin submersible), China (Jiaolong submersible), and Japan have advanced capabilities in manned deep-sea missions.
 
• Samudrayaan will help India achieve technological self-reliance in deep-sea exploration and research.

questions.question: The work 'Snowmelt Runoff Forecasting in Himalayan River Basin' has been taken up by the Central Water Commission (CWC) in association with _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Remote Sensing Centre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Central Water Commission (CWC) has collaborated with the **National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC)** to develop snowmelt runoff forecasting systems in Himalayan river basins.
 
• NRSC is a part of the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** and is responsible for satellite data acquisition and remote sensing applications.
 
• The system uses advanced satellite-based remote sensing technology to monitor snow cover and predict water flow due to snowmelt in Himalayan rivers.
 
• The forecasting system aims to provide accurate data for managing water resources effectively, especially during peak snowmelt periods.
 
• This initiative plays a crucial role in mitigating water-related risks such as floods and ensuring sustainable water management in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC)**

 
 
• NRSC is a key wing of ISRO that specializes in acquiring, processing, and analyzing satellite imagery for various applications.
 
• It is involved in activities such as disaster management, environmental monitoring, and resource planning using remote sensing technologies.
 
• NRSC operates through a network of regional centers across India to cater to localized needs.
 
 
 
• **Snowmelt Runoff**
 
 
• Snowmelt runoff refers to the flow of water resulting from the melting of accumulated snow, particularly in mountainous regions.
 
• This phenomenon is a significant source of freshwater for rivers and streams, especially in regions like the Himalayas.
 
• Accurate forecasting helps in managing water resources and preventing flood risks in downstream areas.
 
 
 
• **Himalayan River Basins**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a dimension measured by the Gender Inequality Index (GII)?

• **Labor market participation** is assessed by the labor force participation rate of women compared to men.

questions.question: What is the region lying to the north of the Narmada River called?
questions.solution:

• The region lying to the north of the Narmada River is referred to as the **Central Highlands**.
 
• The Central Highlands are bounded by the **Aravalli Hills in the northwest** and the Vindhyan Range to the south.
 
• This region is part of the **northern extension of the Peninsular Plateau of India**.
 
• The Central Highlands include the **Malwa Plateau** and parts of Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The rivers in this region primarily flow from the south to the north due to the **slope of the plateau**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Narmada River**

 
 
• The Narmada River is considered the **traditional boundary** separating North and South India.
 
• It flows westward, unlike most other rivers in India, which flow eastward.
 
• The Narmada originates from the **Amarkantak Plateau** in Madhya Pradesh and drains into the Arabian Sea.
 
 
 
• **Vindhyan Range**
 
 
• The Vindhyan Range acts as a **southern boundary for the Central Highlands**.
 
• It is one of the oldest mountain ranges in India, predominantly made of sandstone.
 
• It plays a significant role in separating the Indo-Gangetic Plains from the Deccan Plateau.
 
 
 
• **Aravalli Range**
 
 
• The Aravalli Range, located in northwestern India, is one of the **oldest fold mountains in the world**.
 
• It forms the **northwestern boundary of the Central Highlands**.
 
• The range is known for its rich mineral deposits and biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Peninsular Plateau**
 
 
• The Peninsular Plateau is the **oldest landmass** of India, formed during the Precambrian era.
 
• It is divided into two major parts: the **Central Highlands** and the **Deccan Plateau**.
 
• This plateau is rich in natural resources, including minerals, forests, and fertile soil.

questions.question: In Windows OS, which of the following actions will permanently delete a file without sending it to the Recycle Bin?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pressing **Shift + Delete** bypasses the Recycle Bin and permanently deletes a file from the system.
 
• This action removes the file from the file system table, making it inaccessible to the user unless recovery methods are employed.
 
• The **Recycle Bin** is a feature in Windows OS that stores deleted files temporarily until manually cleared.
 
• Files deleted using **Shift + Delete** cannot be restored through the Recycle Bin.
 
• For accidental permanent deletion, specialized data recovery software may be required to retrieve the file.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Recycle Bin in Windows OS**

 
 
• The Recycle Bin is a special folder where deleted files are temporarily stored.
 
• Users can restore files from the Recycle Bin unless the bin has been emptied or files are deleted permanently using Shift + Delete.
 
• The Recycle Bin can be customized to allocate a specific amount of storage space for deleted files.
 
 
 
• **Permanent Deletion**
 
 
• Permanent deletion bypasses temporary storage locations like the Recycle Bin.
 
• It removes file references from the file system, but the actual data remains on the storage device until overwritten.
 
• Tools like disk shredders can be used to overwrite deleted files, ensuring complete erasure.
 
 
 
• **Data Recovery**
 
 
• Data recovery tools like EaseUS or Recuva can retrieve files that have been deleted permanently, provided the data has not been overwritten.
 
• Recovery is more successful if attempted promptly after deletion.
 
 
 
• **Keyboard Shortcuts in Windows**
 
 
• Shift + Delete: Permanently deletes a file without sending it to the Recycle Bin.
 
• Ctrl + C and Ctrl + V: Copy and paste files or content.
 
• Alt + Tab: Switch between open windows.
 
• Ctrl + Z: Undo the last action.

questions.question: What happens to magnetic fields when a material becomes superconducting and experiences the Meissner effect?

options.text: Magnetic fields are completely expelled from the interior of the material.
Magnetic fields penetrate the material freely.
Magnetic fields are increased in strength within the material.
Magnetic fields are absorbed and stored inside the material.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magnetic fields are completely expelled from the interior of the material.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Meissner effect is a defining property of superconductors where magnetic fields are expelled from the interior of the material during the transition to the superconducting state.
 
• This phenomenon occurs below a critical temperature (Tc) unique to each superconducting material.
 
• The expulsion of magnetic fields is a result of the superconducting material forming perfect diamagnetic properties.
 
• As the superconducting state is achieved, the material cancels the internal magnetic field by generating surface currents that oppose the applied magnetic field.
 
• It is distinct from perfect conductivity, as it implies both zero electrical resistance and zero magnetic field within the material.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Superconductivity:**

 
 
• Superconductivity is a quantum mechanical phenomenon where certain materials exhibit zero electrical resistance and expel magnetic fields below a critical temperature.
 
• It was discovered in 1911 by Heike Kamerlingh Onnes in mercury cooled to 4.2 K.
 
• Applications include MRI machines, particle accelerators, and quantum computing.
 
 
 
• **Meissner Effect:**
 
 
• Named after Walther Meissner and Robert Ochsenfeld, who discovered it in 1933.
 
• It demonstrates the fundamental difference between superconductors and perfect conductors.
 
• The magnetic field is expelled entirely from the bulk of the material, not just reduced.
 
 
 
• **Type I vs Type II Superconductors:**
 
 
• Type I superconductors completely expel magnetic fields and are typically elemental metals.
 
• Type II superconductors allow partial penetration of magnetic fields in the form of vortices and are often alloys or compounds.
 
 
 
• **Critical Temperature (Tc):**
 
 
• The temperature below which a material becomes superconducting.
 
• Varies widely among materials, from below 1 K in some metals to above 100 K in high-temperature superconductors.

questions.question: When were the Municipal Corporations of Calcutta and Bombay established?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1726**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Municipal Corporations of Calcutta (now Kolkata) and Bombay (now Mumbai) were established in the year **1726**.
 
• They were formed under the provisions of the **Charter of 1726**, issued by the British East India Company.
 
• This Charter led to the establishment of a **Mayor's Court** and municipal governance systems in these cities.
 
• The primary objective was to improve urban administration and cater to the needs of a growing British population in these trading hubs.
 
• These were among the earliest attempts at formal municipal governance in India during the colonial period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Charter of 1726:**

 
 
• It was issued by King George I of Britain at the request of the British East India Company.
 
• The Charter introduced a system of civil and criminal courts in the presidency towns of Bombay, Calcutta, and Madras.
 
• This laid the foundation for modern municipal governance in India.
 
 
 
• **Municipal Governance in Colonial India:**
 
 
• The British introduced municipal governance to ensure better administration, sanitation, and urban development in growing cities.
 
• Municipal corporations were primarily established in trading centers like Bombay, Madras, and Calcutta.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Urban Local Bodies:**
 
 
• The Indian Councils Act of 1861 and 1882 further developed local self-governance in India.
 
• In 1882, Lord Ripon, known as the “Father of Local Self-Government in India,” introduced reforms to make municipal bodies more representative.
 
 
 
• **Current Status:**
 
 
• Today, municipal corporations in India operate under the provisions of the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act (1992).
 
• This amendment provides constitutional status to Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) for decentralized governance.

questions.question: Which programme of the Indian Government uses Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) data for identifying beneficiaries?

options.text: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY-G)** is a rural housing scheme aimed at providing pucca houses to economically weaker sections in rural areas.
 
• The scheme uses **Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) data** to identify beneficiaries based on deprivation criteria such as housing conditions, income, and social parameters.
 
• Launched in **2016**, the scheme targets households without housing or living in kutcha houses with zero, one, or two rooms.
 
• The scheme aims to achieve its goal of "Housing for All by 2022" by constructing around 2.95 crore houses in rural areas.
 
• Under PMAY-G, financial assistance of up to **Rs. 1.2 lakh in plain areas** and **Rs. 1.3 lakh in hilly or difficult terrains** is provided to beneficiaries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011:**

 
 
• SECC 2011 was conducted to gather comprehensive data on socio-economic status, income, and caste details of households in India.
 
• The census serves as a critical tool for identifying beneficiaries of various government schemes and programs.
 
• It includes data on housing deprivation, occupational status, and other parameters to ensure targeted interventions.
 
• SECC data is widely used in programs like PMAY-G, Ayushman Bharat, and others to ensure transparency and fairness in beneficiary selection.
 
 
 
• **Housing for All by 2022:**
 
 
• This is a flagship mission launched by the Indian government to address the housing deficit in both urban and rural areas.
 
• It is divided into two components: **PMAY-Urban** for urban areas and **PMAY-Gramin** for rural areas.
 
• The initiative aims to provide affordable housing to all eligible beneficiaries, ensuring access to basic amenities like water, sanitation, and electricity.
 
 
 
• **Deprivation Criteria:**
 
 
• Under PMAY-G, SECC data identifies beneficiaries based on deprivation indicators such as households without housing or living in kutcha houses.
 
• These criteria ensure that the scheme targets the most vulnerable and needy sections of society.
 
 
 
• **Implementation Process:**
 
 
• PMAY-G is implemented in partnership with state governments and local bodies to ensure timely completion of projects.
 
• Funds are transferred directly to the beneficiaries' accounts through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
 
• Beneficiaries are encouraged to participate in the construction process to reduce costs and ensure quality.

questions.question: 'The Flying Apsara' painting is a masterpiece in which of the following caves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ajanta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **'The Flying Apsara'** is a famous painting located in the **Ajanta Caves**, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Maharashtra, India.
 
• Ajanta Caves are renowned for their exquisite **Buddhist rock-cut architecture** and paintings depicting Jataka tales and the life of Buddha.
 
• 'The Flying Apsara' painting showcases the **elegance and intricate artistry** of ancient Indian painters, emphasizing movement and grace.
 
• The Ajanta frescoes are painted using the **tempera technique**, combining natural pigments and plant-based adhesives to create enduring artworks.
 
• The caves date back to **2nd century BCE to 6th century CE**, representing one of the finest examples of Indian classical art traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ajanta Caves:**

 
 
• The Ajanta Caves consist of 30 caves, including monasteries and prayer halls, carved into the rock face of a horseshoe-shaped cliff.
 
• The caves are primarily dedicated to **Buddhism** and were used by monks for meditation and teaching.
 
• They are an important cultural and historical site, preserving ancient Indian art, architecture, and religious practices.
 
 
 
• **Artistic Techniques:**
 
 
• The tempera technique used in Ajanta paintings involves mixing pigments with a binding agent such as gum or egg yolk.
 
• The artists employed natural light in the caves, which filtered through openings, to work on the intricate details.
 
• The paintings depict themes like **Buddhist myths, deities, and daily life activities**, showcasing the harmony between religion and art.
 
 
 
• **Apsaras in Indian Art:**
 
 
• Apsaras are celestial maidens or dancers in Indian mythology, often associated with grace, beauty, and divine energy.
 
• 'The Flying Apsara' painting symbolizes the **dynamic movement and ethereal presence** of these celestial beings.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Status:**
 
 
• The Ajanta Caves were designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in **1983**.
 
• They are recognized for their historical importance and artistic achievement, drawing visitors and scholars from around the world.

questions.question: What is the temperature of the triple point of water on the Celsius scale?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.01ºC**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The triple point of water is the temperature and pressure at which water exists simultaneously in its **solid, liquid, and gaseous states**.
 
• On the Celsius scale, the triple point of water is precisely **0.01ºC**.
 
• This value is used as a standard fixed point in the definition of the Celsius temperature scale.
 
• The corresponding pressure at the triple point of water is exactly **611.657 pascals (Pa)**.
 
• The triple point of water is critical for scientific calibration of thermometers and maintaining the International Temperature Scale.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Definition of Triple Point:**

 
 
• The triple point is a unique thermodynamic state where three phases (solid, liquid, and gas) coexist in equilibrium.
 
• It is a fundamental reference point for thermodynamic measurements.
 
 
 
• **Kelvin and Celsius Relationship:**
 
 
• The triple point of water is defined as 273.16 K on the Kelvin scale.
 
• The Celsius scale is defined such that the triple point of water is 0.01ºC.
 
 
 
• **Role in Metrology:**
 
 
• The triple point of water is used in metrology to calibrate temperature-measuring instruments.
 
• It is a key reference point for defining the International Temperature Scale (ITS-90).
 
 
 
• **Physical Significance:**
 
 
• The triple point demonstrates the delicate balance of thermodynamic states under specific conditions.
 
• For water, it highlights the unique properties of this universal solvent, which is critical for life on Earth.

questions.question: Harappan seals were made mostly from which of the following?

__
 
• Harappan seals were primarily made of **steatite**, a soft stone that was easy to carve and shape.
 
• Steatite seals were often heated to harden them, which also gave them a glazed finish.
 
• The seals typically featured inscriptions in the **Harappan script** along with depictions of animals, humans, or religious symbols.
 
• These seals were used for **trade and administrative purposes**, serving as markers of ownership or identity.
 
• Thousands of such seals have been discovered at major Harappan sites like Mohenjo-Daro and Harappa, providing valuable insights into the civilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Steatite:** Also known as soapstone, steatite is a type of metamorphic rock composed mainly of talc. It is soft and can be easily carved, making it ideal for creating intricate designs.
 
• **Harappan Script:** The writing on Harappan seals remains undeciphered to this day. It consists of pictorial symbols and is believed to represent an ancient form of writing.
 
• **Animal Motifs:** Common animals depicted on seals include bulls, unicorns, elephants, and rhinoceroses. These may have had symbolic or religious significance.
 
• **Usage of Seals:** Apart from trade, the seals might have been used to stamp clay on goods or letters, serving as a form of identity verification or branding.
 
• **Archaeological Importance:** Harappan seals provide critical evidence of the technological, artistic, and social aspects of the Indus Valley Civilization, one of the world's oldest urban cultures.

questions.question: What happens when you press Ctrl + S while working on a document in computer system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Saves the current document**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pressing **Ctrl + S** in most computer applications is the universal shortcut for saving the current document or file.
 
• This shortcut command is commonly used in software like **Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and other text or file editors**.
 
• It ensures that any changes made to the document are stored in the permanent memory (like the hard drive) to avoid data loss.
 
• If the document has not been saved previously, the system will prompt the user to **choose a file name and location** for saving.
 
• Regularly saving your work using **Ctrl + S** is a good practice to prevent loss of data due to unexpected crashes or errors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Keyboard Shortcuts:**

 
 
• Keyboard shortcuts are combinations of keys that provide quick access to common functions in applications.
 
• For example, **Ctrl + C** is used to copy, **Ctrl + V** to paste, and **Ctrl + Z** to undo the last action.
 
• These shortcuts help improve productivity and reduce reliance on mouse clicks.
 
 
 
• **Save vs Save As:**
 
 
• The **Save** command updates the current file with any changes made, while **Save As** allows saving the file under a new name or in a different location.
 
• Save As is particularly useful when creating multiple versions of a document.
 
 
 
• **AutoSave Feature:**
 
 
• Many modern applications include an AutoSave feature that periodically saves the document in the background.
 
• This feature minimizes data loss in case of system crashes or power outages.
 
• For example, Microsoft Office applications have AutoSave enabled for files stored in OneDrive or SharePoint.
 
 
 
• **File Formats:**
 
 
• When saving a document, users can choose from various file formats such as **.docx, .pdf, .txt, or .xls**, depending on the software.
 
• Each format serves a specific purpose—for instance, **.pdf** is often used for read-only sharing, while **.docx** is editable.

questions.question: The famous 'Trimurti' sculpture is present in which of the following caves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Elephanta caves**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Trimurti' sculpture is located in the **Elephanta Caves**, a UNESCO World Heritage Site near Mumbai, Maharashtra.
 
• The sculpture depicts the **three faces of Lord Shiva**, representing his roles as the Creator (Brahma), Preserver (Vishnu), and Destroyer (Mahesh).
 
• This colossal statue is carved in relief, measuring approximately **20 feet in height**, and is considered one of the finest examples of ancient Indian rock-cut art.
 
• The Elephanta Caves date back to the **5th–7th century CE**, and the Trimurti is the central figure of the main cave, known as the Great Cave or Cave 1.
 
• The caves are attributed to the **Shaivite faith** and reflect the rich cultural and religious heritage of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Elephanta Caves:**

 
 
• Located on Elephanta Island (Gharapuri Island) in Mumbai Harbour, about 10 km from the Gateway of India.
 
• These caves are divided into two groups: **Hindu caves** (dedicated to Lord Shiva) and **Buddhist caves**.
 
• The island was named "Elephanta" by Portuguese explorers after they found a large stone elephant statue there.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Trimurti:**
 
 
• The Trimurti embodies the concept of the cosmic functions of creation, preservation, and destruction in Hinduism.
 
• The three heads symbolize **Satvik (purity), Rajasik (passion), and Tamasik (destruction)** aspects of existence.
 
 
 
• **Artistic Style:**
 
 
• The caves are an excellent example of **Gupta-era architecture**, showcasing intricate carvings and iconography.
 
• The Trimurti relief is considered a masterpiece of Indian art and is an iconic representation of rock-cut sculpture.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO Recognition:**
 
 
• The Elephanta Caves were designated as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in 1987 for their outstanding universal value.
 
• They are preserved as an important cultural heritage of India.

• Aparna Sen, a renowned Indian filmmaker, received the **Satyajit Ray Lifetime Achievement Award** in January 2025.
 
• The award honors her exceptional contributions to Indian cinema as a director, screenwriter, and actress.
 
• She is known for her critically acclaimed films, such as **"36 Chowringhee Lane" (1981)**, which received a National Film Award.
 
• Aparna Sen has been a significant figure in parallel cinema, focusing on social issues and human relationships in her works.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Satyajit Ray**

 
 
• Satyajit Ray was a renowned Indian filmmaker known for his contributions to world cinema.
 
• His famous works include the **Apu Trilogy**, "Charulata," and "Pather Panchali."
 
• He received an **Honorary Academy Award** in 1992 for his lifetime achievements.
 
• Ray's films often explored human emotions, social realities, and cultural nuances.

• Aparna Sen started her career as an actress before transitioning to filmmaking.
 
• She has directed notable films like **"Mr. and Mrs. Iyer" (2002)** and "The Japanese Wife" (2010).
 
• She has received multiple National Film Awards for her contributions to Indian cinema.
 
• Her works often highlight women-centric narratives and societal challenges.

• It is presented at the **International Film Festival of India (IFFI)**, held in Goa.
 
• Past recipients include filmmakers such as Martin Scorsese and István Szabó.
 
• This award celebrates the legacy of Satyajit Ray, a pioneer of Indian cinema.
 
 
 
• **Parallel Cinema in India**
 
 
• Parallel cinema, also known as art cinema, focuses on realistic and socially conscious themes.
 
• Filmmakers like Aparna Sen, Satyajit Ray, and Shyam Benegal have contributed significantly to this movement.
 
• It emerged as an alternative to mainstream Bollywood cinema in the 1950s.
 
• Parallel cinema often highlights critical social issues, human relationships, and cultural narratives.
